newsitem.title: CANADA: Cineplex says projectionists reject deal.
newsitem.headline: Cineplex says projectionists reject deal.

text.p: Cineplex Odeon Corp said on Friday locked-out projectionists rejected an agreement to settle a nearly four-month-old labor dispute.

Members of Local 173 of the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) voted against a new deal reached between Cineplex and the union bargaining committee, Cineplex said in a statement.
The projectionists have been locked out since October 26.
"We are disappointed that the members of Local 173 rejected Cineplex Odeon's new offer", said Howard Lichtman, executive vice president of marketing and communications.
Cineplex said the new contract offered full-time employment to 53 employees, down from an estimated 70 to 75 full-time jobs.
The new deal offered wages ranging from C$14 to C$16 per hour. Based on a 40-hour work week, annual wages would range between C$29,120 to C$33,280 plus benefits.

"This is an 11 percent wage reduction from their current average salary of C$30,000 to C$40,000 per year, but is consistent with the industry standard throughout North America," Cineplex said. The company also offered a C$1,000 signing bonus to returning projectionists.
Cineplex said employees who lost their jobs would be offered up to 26 weeks of severance pay.
Union officials were unavailable for comment on Friday.
Lichtman said the company will not revise its offer.
"Our final offer is on the table," he said in a telephone interview.
